newsitem.title: CANADA: Deal seen in British Columbia lumber labor dispute.
newsitem.headline: Deal seen in British Columbia lumber labor dispute.

text.p: British Columbia's forestry companies and the union representing coastal lumber workers are getting closer to a deal on a new contract, the chief negotiator for the companies said Tuesday.

"Things went pretty well. They have moved, we have moved. We're inching closer together," said Keith Bennett, chief negotiator for 65 forestry companies who bargain as Forest Industrial Relations, after talks Tuesday.
The negotiations were the first since the companies broke off talks last Friday when wildcat strikes hit International Forest Products Ltd. Discussions were rescheduled after the strikes ended.
Bennett said he thought a deal on a new contract could be just days away. The current contract expired June 14.

Officials for the IWA-Canada union which represents the workers were not immediately available for comment. But IWA-Canada president Dave Haggard said last week that a contract accord was perhaps less than a week away.
Bennett said after Tuesday's talks that the two sides remained divided on the issue of wages, but the gap had narrowed.

The companies have sweetened their offer to include wage increases totalling four percent over three years, while the union has lowered its demand to around seven percent over the same period, Bennett said.
